name: Question 16
worked_solution:
Here, both the lower and upper limits contain a variable. However, to apply FTC II, we need the variable to be on the upper limit only. So, we can split the integral into two integrals, and rewrite them so that in both cases the variable is on the upper limit. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-{x}^{3}}^{x}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{-{x}^{3}}^{a}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{a}^{x}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-{\int }_{a}^{-{x}^{3}}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{a}^{x}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\end{aligned}
$$

where $a$ is any constant number between $-{x}^{3}$ and $x.$

The integrand ${t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ is continuous for all $t,$ so applying the FTC II gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{\int }_{a}^{-{x}^{3}}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{a}^{x}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\int }_{a}^{-{x}^{3}}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\int }_{a}^{x}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({\int }_{a}^{u}{t}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t)+{x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-(-3{x}^{2}){u}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡u+{x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =3{x}^{2}{(-{x}^{3})}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-{x}^{3})+{x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =3{x}^{14}\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{3}+{x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the substitution $u=-{x}^{3}.$

Finally, we can compute ${f}^{′}(1).$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1) & =3(1)^{14}\operatorname{cos}⁡{1}^{3}+{1}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡1 \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡1+\operatorname{cos}⁡1 \\  & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡1.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 16
?

Find f′(1) if f(x)=∫−x3xt4cos⁡tdt.

a
0
b
−2
c
1
d
2−cos⁡1
e
4cos⁡1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, both the lower and upper limits contain a variable. However, to apply FTC II, we need the variable to be on the upper limit only. So, we can split the integral into two integrals, and rewrite them so that in both cases the variable is on the upper limit. We get ∫−x3xt4cos⁡tdt=∫−x3at4cos⁡tdt+∫axt4cos⁡tdt=−∫a−x3t4cos⁡tdt+∫axt4cos⁡tdt, where a is any constant number between −x3 and x.

The integrand t4cos⁡t is continuous for all t, so applying the FTC II gives f′(x)=ddx(−∫a−x3t4cos⁡tdt+∫axt4cos⁡tdt)=−ddx(∫a−x3t4cos⁡tdt)+ddx(∫axt4cos⁡tdt)=−dudxddu(∫aut4cos⁡tdt)+x4cos⁡x=−(−3x2)u4cos⁡u+x4cos⁡x=3x2(−x3)4cos⁡(−x3)+x4cos⁡x=3x14cos⁡x3+x4cos⁡x.

Note that we used the substitution u=−x3.

Finally, we can compute f′(1). We get f′(1)=3(1)14cos⁡13+14cos⁡1=3cos⁡1+cos⁡1=4cos⁡1.
